summary: Rich-Text Popup Messages v2 backend fully verified via pytest (14/14 PASS). Sanitizer blocks <script>/onerror/javascript:/iframe/style-injection XSS vectors; anchors auto-decorated with target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer; YouTube ID parsed correctly from watch/youtu.be/embed URLs; multi-CTA order preserved; PUT replaces cta_buttons array atomically and enabling one popup auto-disables others. Public GET /api/admin/popup/active works without auth and returns all new fields (message_html, image_url, youtube_url, youtube_id, cta_buttons). Upload endpoint: admin auth accepted (200), no-auth = 401, regular-user token = 403, oversize (>5MB) rejected 400, bad extension rejected 400. Frontend admin panel rendered and interactive: /admin/popup-messages page loads, `admin-popup-new-btn` opens form + side-by-side live preview (`admin-popup-form` + `admin-popup-preview`), title input updates preview in real-time, CTA add/remove/max-3-disabled works. TipTap editor mounts with all toolbar buttons (bold/italic/underline/h2/h3/bullets/numbers/link/undo/redo). Playwright keyboard typing into contenteditable with rapid toolbar clicks had race conditions that made deep formatting E2E flaky — code inspection confirms wiring is correct (onUpdate emits getHTML into formData.message_html which flows to PopupPreviewCard via dangerouslySetInnerHTML). Backend tests are the authoritative correctness check for the sanitizer & shape.

minor.issue: Small images (<800 wide) are only 16:9-cropped, NOT upscaled to 800x450. Spec/PRD says 'auto-normalized to 16:9 800x450 JPEG' but code only downsizes when img.size[0] > 800 (admin_popup_routes.py L380-381). 400x300 input yields 400x225 output. Aspect ratio is correct; absolute size is not. Low priority — end-user popup renderer uses w-full anyway.

bleach strip=True removes the <script> element but preserves inner text ('alert(1)' remains as visible text in message_html). Not exploitable (rendered as text, never executed) but shows raw XSS payload text to end-users. Consider using bleach's strip_comments + Cleaner with strip=True OR post-process to drop script/style text content entirely.

action_items: OPTIONAL: main agent may want to upscale small uploaded images to exactly 800x450 to match spec (currently only downsizes) — one-liner: `if img.size != (800,450): img = img.resize((800,450), Image.LANCZOS)` after the crop, regardless of original width.

OPTIONAL: consider stripping inner text of disallowed tags (script/style) so users don't see raw JS-looking payload text if an admin ever pastes it. e.g., pre-strip tags with content: `raw = re.sub(r'<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>', '', raw, flags=re.I|re.S)` before bleach.
Retest not needed unless spec strictness on 800x450 exact dimensions is enforced.
critical_code_review_comments: admin_popup_routes.py L380: only resizes DOWN — spec says 800x450 exact; small images bypass resize. Consider unconditional resize to (800,450) after 16:9 crop.

admin_popup_routes.py sanitize_html: regex-based post-processing of <a> tags after bleach can be fragile against edge cases (e.g., <a\n href=...>). Consider using bleach's built-in `set_attributes` callback or `linkify` for safer link handling.

PopupEditor.js: TipTap Link.configure has openOnClick: false (correct for admin editor), but no URL validation before setLink() call. A malicious admin could still enter javascript:... URL in the prompt — server sanitizer catches it, but client-side UX would still show the anchor in the preview. Low priority.
AdminPopupMessages.js uploadImage(): does not clear image_url on error; uses `d.detail || d.message`, but FastAPI 401/403 returns {detail: '...'} which is correctly handled. OK.

PopupPreviewCard uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML with unsanitized formData.message_html straight from the TipTap editor (client-side). This is safe today because TipTap only generates whitelisted tags, but if extensions change (e.g., raw HTML paste allowed), preview could render XSS locally. Not a security issue since it's admin-only, but worth noting.

Backend `/api/admin/popup/create` returns `success:false` with status 200 on server errors (see except block L234-236). Downstream tests can't rely on non-200 status codes to detect failure — consider raising HTTPException(500) instead of returning success:false.
